Any ambient cap containing an endpoint pays at least its ordinary depth, and either endpoint's prescribed continuous cap extends by finite base tilt to exclude the two other compact fibers. The finite maximum is positive somewhere on this open ray exactly if one branch is strictly positive at its boundary or has positive slope. This treats an equality at the boundary and zero eventual slope correctly.

The explicit H_i determines each full-at-minimum branch with equality of both choices at a tie. The all-proper case yields the stated weighted inequality.

For u=0,v=1, the actual nonnegative loss makes the full-at-minimum hinge argument 2L+k_i e_i≥0. Thus θ^∞ represents a valid inverse branch even at a tie, and L(0,1)=𝒥_{θ^∞}(q) equals the largest slope parameter from the envelope. Q>rb gives the tied-endpoint derivative inequality automatically. The strict B-only threshold is exactly 𝒥_{θ^∞}>drb.
